title: Quotations on the manor, the Black Death, the labour laws, debasement and Oresme's De moneta (Chapter 11)
source: Bland, Brown & Tawney (eds.), English Economic History: Select Documents (1914); Statutes of the Realm, vol. 1 (1810); N. de Wailly, Mémoire sur les variations de la livre tournois (1857); N. Oresme, De moneta, ed. L. Wolowski (1864); Rolnick, Velde & Weber (1996/1997); Clark (c. 1999 working paper; 2016 abstract); Humphries & Weisdorf (2019, accepted manuscript); Ashraf & Galor (NBER WP 17037, 2011)
series: one row per quoted fact: id, dynasty (here: country), year, year_note, value, unit, numeral (unused), file (key of sources below), juan (part.section.number of a document, chapter or page), quote (verbatim), note
license: Short quotations only, for comment and teaching. The 1810, 1857, 1864 and 1914 texts are in the public domain (the 1914 collection is Project Gutenberg eBook #43211); the modern papers are quoted, not copied.
notes: Every downloadable document was fetched in the shell on 2026-10-13 and the rows from bbt1914, clark1999wp, clark2016, hw2019, ag2011 and vv2013 were found verbatim in the extracted text; data/fetch/verify_web_quotes.py repeats the check. The rows from sotr1810, wailly1857, oresme1864 and rvw1997 were read by eye on the page images (format image), because their OCR text is too corrupt (the 1810, 1857 and 1864 scans) or merges the two columns of the page (the 1997 reprint); they are counted but not checked by the script. Page references: bbt1914 rows give part, section and number of the document with its first page in the 1914 edition (the Gutenberg text has no page markers); rvw1997 rows give the printed page of the Quarterly Review; clark1999wp rows give the page of the PDF. Discrepancies kept visible: (1) the South Frith receiver's account of 1349–50 itemizes defects of rent that add to 118s 10¼d, 5d less than the total of 119s 3¼d it states; the chapter uses only the stated totals (119s 3¼d − 15s 4d = 103s 11¼d, as the account says). (2) The 1349 Ordinance takes as its standard the wages of the twentieth year of the reign (1346–7) 'or in the five or six common years last preceding'; the 1351 Statute says 'the said Twentieth Year, or Four Years before' for farm servants. (3) Rolnick, Velde & Weber's text gives the Crown's seigniorage share during the Great Debasement as 25 percent, their Table 3 as 26 percent (1544–47); the chapter uses the table (snapshot rvw1996_mint_revenue). (4) Clark's working paper (c. 1999) finds no efficiency effect of the Black Death, his 2016 article finds a temporary efficiency gain; both are quoted and the chapter says which is which. (5) The Avalon Project's page titled 'The Statute of Laborers; 1351' prints the 1349 Ordinance (addressed to the archbishop, dated in the twenty-third year of the reign); it is not used. The 1349 Ordinance is quoted in the translation of Bland, Brown & Tawney; the 1351 Statute in the English translation printed beside the French text in the Statutes of the Realm. Latin quotations from Oresme are given as printed in Wolowski's edition, with its spelling (monete, monetæ).
